metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Paden City, WV
metaDescription: Paden City, Tyler County mineral owners: Sistersville-adjacent boom-era deed history, Marcellus/Utica units, and multi-generation heir splits.
heroLead: Paden City sits near Sistersville's historic oil-boom ground in Tyler County, where 1890s-era deed history and modern horizontal units both apply to the surrounding acreage.
intro: Just up the Ohio River from Sistersville, Paden City shares in the dense oil-era deed record that boomtown generated, while also sitting within reach of the Marcellus and Utica/Point Pleasant horizontal development that's spread through Tyler County over the past decade and a half.

sections.heading: Sharing in Sistersville's historic deed density
paragraphs: Paden City-area tracts were often swept into the same wave of leasing and re-leasing that accompanied Sistersville's oil boom, meaning a mineral interest here can have a deed history running back further than a typical rural West Virginia parcel, with more transactions to trace along the way.

sections.heading: Modern development on the same acreage
paragraphs: Where Paden City-area tracts have been drawn into newer Marcellus or Utica/Point Pleasant units, the pro-rata royalty share depends on the original tract's surface acreage relative to the current unit — a figure that should come from the filed unit plat, not an assumption based on the tract's historical size before pooling.

sections.heading: Sorting boom-era assignments from current lease terms
paragraphs: Because Paden City-area tracts share in Sistersville's dense oil-boom deed history, it's common to find multiple historical assignments recorded against a single interest, some from the 1890s and some from more recent Marcellus-era leasing. Only the most recent, currently-in-force lease actually governs today's royalty terms.
A title review sorts the historical record from the operative lease, which is essential before valuing an interest that's changed hands this many times.

faqs.question: Does Paden City share Sistersville's older deed history?
faqs.answer: Largely, yes — the two communities sit close enough along the Ohio River that much of the oil-boom era leasing activity touched both areas.

faqs.question: Is my Paden City tract in a Marcellus or Utica unit?
faqs.answer: Possibly either or both, given Tyler County's stacked-pay geology. Checking your division orders and unit filings will confirm.

faqs.question: How many heirs typically hold a Paden City-area family interest?
faqs.answer: Given the depth of the deed history here, interests split among a dozen or more descendants across several generations are common.

faqs.question: Which lease governs my Paden City interest if there have been several over the years?
faqs.answer: Only the most recent, currently-in-force lease controls; a title review identifies which one that is.

faqs.question: Does living outside Tyler County make it harder for my family to sell a Paden City interest?
faqs.answer: No, out-of-state heirs sell documented fractional interests to us regularly; the title work happens at the courthouse regardless of where the heir currently lives.
